easy.def: A ghost.
examples: The story has a phantom.
The phantom floated down the hall.
We read about a phantom.

more.def: A ghost, or something that seems real but is not.
examples: The story is about a phantom that haunts the old theater.
A phantom shape drifted through the foggy graveyard.
In the tale, a phantom appeared at midnight and then faded away.

easy.def: A king of ancient Egypt.
examples: The pharaoh ruled Egypt.
A pharaoh lived in a palace.
We read about a pharaoh.

more.def: A ruler of ancient Egypt, who was thought of as a god by the people.
examples: The pharaoh ruled ancient Egypt from a palace beside the Nile.
The great pyramids were built as tombs for pharaohs.
The pharaoh wore a gold crown and carried a staff.

easy.def: A place where you get medicine.
examples: Mom went to the pharmacy.
The pharmacy is open.
I got medicine at the pharmacy.

more.def: A shop or part of a store where medicine is prepared and sold.
examples: Mom picked up my medicine at the pharmacy.
The pharmacy is next to the grocery store.
The pharmacist at the pharmacy answered our questions.

easy.def: One stage of something that changes.
examples: The moon is in a new phase.
This is a new phase.
The first phase is done.

more.def: One of the steps or stages of something that changes over time.
examples: The moon goes through many phases each month.
A caterpillar is one phase in a butterfly's life.
The first phase of the project is finished.

easy.def: Very, very good.
examples: She is a phenomenal singer.
It was a phenomenal game.
A phenomenal job.

more.def: Amazing and much better than usual.
examples: She is a phenomenal singer with a voice that fills the whole room.
The team played a phenomenal game and won by twenty points.
His memory is phenomenal; he can recall every word of the book.

easy.def: Something that happens that you can see.
examples: A rainbow is a phenomenon.
The eclipse is a phenomenon.
We studied a phenomenon.

more.def: Something that happens or exists in nature or society, especially something unusual that can be observed.
examples: A rainbow is a natural phenomenon caused by sunlight and rain.
The northern lights are a beautiful phenomenon in the night sky.
The game became a phenomenon, and everyone was playing it.

easy.def: A word you say when you are glad something bad did not happen.
examples: Phew! I am glad that is over.
Phew, it is hot.
Phew, we made it!

more.def: A word used to show that you feel relieved, tired or hot.
examples: Phew! I am glad the test is over.
Phew, it is hot in here!
Phew, we got to the bus just in time.

easy.def: A person who thinks about big questions in life.
examples: The philosopher wrote a book.
A philosopher asked big questions.
He is a philosopher.

more.def: A person who thinks deeply and writes about big questions, such as what is right, what is true and how people should live.
examples: A famous philosopher from ancient Greece asked what it means to be good.
The philosopher wrote a book about how people should treat each other.
My uncle is a philosopher who teaches at a college.

easy.def: Big ideas about life and how to live.
examples: He studies philosophy.
Her philosophy is to be kind.
The book is about philosophy.

more.def: The study of big questions about life, such as what is right and wrong, or a person's own set of beliefs about how to live.
examples: Philosophy asks big questions, like what it means to be fair.
My grandfather's philosophy is to try your best and be kind.
She studied philosophy at college and read the works of old thinkers.

easy.def: A tool you use to talk to people far away.
examples: The phone rang.
I talk on the phone.
Mom has a phone.

more.def: A device that lets you talk to people who are far away.
examples: I called my grandmother on the phone.
The phone rang, and my dad answered it.
She used her phone to take a picture of the rainbow.

easy.def: Fake.
examples: The money was phony.
He gave a phony name.
The phony smile was clear.

more.def: Not real, and meant to trick people.
examples: The phony money was easy to spot.
He gave a phony name at the door.
Her phony smile hid her worry.

easy.def: A picture taken with a camera.
examples: I took a photo.
The photo is pretty.
Look at the photo.

more.def: A picture made with a camera, either printed or kept on a device.
examples: I took a photo of the sunset.
Grandma has a photo of me on the wall.
The photo shows our whole family.

easy.def: A picture made with a camera.
examples: I took a photograph of my cat.
The photograph is on the wall.
This photograph shows our trip.

more.def: A picture taken with a camera.
examples: The photograph shows our family at the beach.
She hung a framed photograph of her grandmother on the wall.
The photograph captured the sunset in bright colors.

easy.def: A person who takes pictures with a camera.
examples: The photographer took our picture.
A photographer works with a camera.
The photographer smiled.

more.def: A person who takes photographs, often as a job.
examples: The photographer took pictures at the wedding.
A nature photographer waited for the deer.
The school photographer lined us up.

easy.def: Having to do with photos.
examples: She has a photographic memory.
A photographic print.
Photographic paper.

more.def: Having to do with photographs, or very exact, like a photograph.
examples: She has a photographic memory and can recall every page.
The shop sells photographic paper and frames.
The artist painted with photographic detail.

easy.def: Taking pictures with a camera.
examples: I like photography.
Photography is fun.
He studies photography.

more.def: The art or hobby of taking pictures with a camera.
examples: I love photography and take pictures of birds.
She studies photography and has a good camera.
Photography lets you save memories of special days.

easy.def: A short group of words.
examples: "In the park" is a phrase.
Say the phrase again.
The phrase is easy to learn.

more.def: A small group of words that go together but are not a whole sentence.
examples: "On the hill" is a phrase.
She repeated the phrase to learn it.
The poem has a lovely phrase about the moon.

easy.def: Having to do with your body.
examples: Running is a physical activity.
Exercise is good for your physical health.
He has a physical job.

more.def: Having to do with the body, or with real things that you can touch.
examples: Gym class is a time for physical exercise.
A broken arm is a physical injury.
A rock is a physical object, but a dream is not.

easy.def: A doctor.
examples: The physician examined me.
A physician works in the hospital.
The physician gave advice.

more.def: A person who is trained to treat sick people, a doctor.
examples: The physician examined my throat.
The family physician gave me a checkup.
The physician told her to rest.

easy.def: The study of things like motion, light and heat.
examples: I like physics.
Physics explains how things move.
He studies physics.

more.def: The science that studies matter, energy, motion, heat and light.
examples: I like physics, because it explains how things move.
A pendulum swinging back and forth is an example of physics.
She is a physics teacher.
